pages.text: One sunny afternoon, <name> and his friends decided to have a rickshaw race in the neighborhood. Each friend hopped onto their colorful rickshaw, decorated with ribbons, bells, and even a little stuffed monkey.

“Ready, set, go!” shouted Meera, waving a flag. The rickshaws zoomed down the street, squeaking and wobbling. <name> laughed as his rickshaw wobbled too, making funny “Wobble-wobble!” noises with every turn.
Suddenly, Ravi’s rickshaw tipped slightly as he tried a sharp turn. He tumbled softly into a pile of pillows Mom had left on the porch, bouncing like a cartoon character. Everyone giggled.

Then, a friendly goat appeared, standing right in the middle of the road. The rickshaws screeched to a stop. The goat stared, chewing grass and refusing to move. <name> waved his hands. “Excuse me, Mr. Goat! Can we pass?” The goat blinked and trotted away slowly, making everyone laugh even harder.
Rival friend Aarav tried sneaky tricks, tossing water balloons at the rickshaws, but they mostly hit the air or bounced harmlessly off a wheel. <name> ducked and shouted, “Nice try!”

The race continued, full of twists, wobbles, and giggles. At the finish line, nobody cared who came first. Mom appeared with cookies and juice, and the friends shared treats, telling funny stories about the goat, the tipped rickshaw, and the sneaky water balloons. <name> felt proud — not for winning, but for the great adventure and giggles shared with friends.
